q: What is Figure A called?
n: Figure A is a 45° elbow, which turns a pipe run by 45 degrees. Source: ASME B16.3 (malleable iron threaded fittings).

q: What is Figure B called?
n: Figure B is a pipe clamp, which supports and secures pipes to walls or structure. Source: MSS SP-58 (pipe hangers and supports).

q: What is Figure C called?
n: Figure C is a towel rack, a bathroom accessory with bars for hanging towels. Source: Bathroom accessory manufacturer literature.

q: What is Figure D called?
n: Figure D is a shower (mixing) valve, which controls hot and cold water flow and temperature to the shower head. Source: ASME A112.18.1 (plumbing supply fittings).

q: What is Figure E called?
n: The AUTO. SPKR marking identifies a fire department (Siamese) connection for an automatic sprinkler system, through which the fire service pumps water in. Source: NFPA 13 / NFPA 14; RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019.

q: What is the material composition of Figure A?
n: Figure A is a threaded galvanized iron (G.I.) elbow, the zinc-coated steel fitting used in water lines. Source: ASTM A53 / ASME B16.3.

q: What is the material composition of Figure B?
n: Figure B is stainless steel, a chromium alloy with a bright, non-magnetic-looking finish that resists corrosion, used for fittings and accessories in wet areas. Source: ASTM A240; plumbing fitting manufacturer literature.

q: What is the material composition of Figure C?
n: Figure C is brass (a copper–zinc alloy) with a yellow-gold color, used for valves, faucets and threaded fittings. Source: ASTM B16/B584 (brass); plumbing fitting manufacturer literature.

q: What is the material composition of Figure D?
n: Figure D is copper, reddish-brown and joined by soldering or brazing, used for water supply and refrigerant lines. Source: ASTM B88 (copper water tube).

q: What is the material composition of Figure E?
n: Figure E is PVC, a light-colored plastic pipe joined with solvent cement, used for drainage and water lines. Source: ASTM D1785 / D2665 (PVC pipe).

q: Which figure is used for waste disposal?
n: Figure C is a food waste disposer, mounted under the kitchen sink to grind food scraps into the drain. Source: ASSE 1008 (food waste disposers); manufacturer literature.

q: Which figure shows a tailpiece?
n: Figure A is a tailpiece, the short straight pipe from the fixture drain outlet down to the trap. Source: ASME A112.18.2 (waste fittings).

q: Which figure is used for washing dishes?
n: Figure D is the kitchen sink, used for washing dishes. A kitchen sink is wider and deeper than a lavatory, with a strainer outlet sized for dishwashing waste. Source: ASME A112.19 (plumbing fixtures).

q: Which figure represents a standard basin?
n: Figure E is a standard lavatory basin for washing hands and face. A lavatory is the smaller wash basin found in toilets and baths, typically with an overflow and a pop-up drain. Source: ASME A112.19.

q: Which figure is used for washing clothes?
n: Figure B is a laundry tub (deep sink), used for washing clothes. A laundry tub is a deep, sturdy sink, often concrete or plastic, used for soaking and hand-washing clothes. Source: ASME A112.19.

q: What device in Figure A is used to instantly heat water at the point of use, commonly in showers?
n: A single-point (instantaneous) water heater heats water on demand right at the outlet, typically at the shower. Source: Water heater manufacturer literature; IEC 60335-2-35.

q: What valve in Figure B is typically installed underground to control water flow from a main line, often for maintenance shut-off?
n: A curb stop is a buried valve on the service line near the property line (curb), turned with a key through a curb box to shut off the supply. Source: AWWA C800 (service line valves); National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: What equipment in Figure C uses sunlight to heat water for domestic use, often mounted on rooftops?
n: A solar water heater uses rooftop collectors to absorb sunlight and heat water for domestic use. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Applications (solar energy use).

q: What device in Figure D prevents pipe damage and noise by absorbing sudden changes in water pressure?
n: A water hammer arrestor has an air or gas cushion that absorbs the pressure surge when a valve closes quickly, preventing banging and pipe damage. Source: PDI-WH 201 (water hammer arresters); National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: What mechanism in Figure E automatically regulates water level in tanks by opening and closing the inlet valve?
n: A float valve opens the tank inlet when the water level drops and closes it as the float rises, keeping the level constant automatically. Source: Plumbing fixture and tank manufacturer literature.

q: What type of pipe is best used for grease traps?
n: Grease traps receive hot, fatty and often acidic kitchen waste, so stainless steel is best: it resists corrosion and cleans easily. Source: PDI-G101 (grease interceptors); manufacturer literature.

q: Which fitting raises water pressure at the outlet?
n: A reducer narrows the pipe. Squeezing the same flow into a smaller outlet raises its velocity and the force (pressure) of the stream at the outlet. Source: Fluid mechanics (continuity equation); plumbing fitting references.

q: What is a 180° pipe bend called?
n: A return bend is a 180° fitting that reverses the direction of a pipe run. Source: ASME B16.3/B16.9 (pipe fittings).

q: Which fitting joins two pipes that can't be turned, using two threaded ends drawn together by a threaded center nut?
n: A union joins two pipes that cannot be rotated. Its two threaded ends are drawn together by a central nut, so the joint can be opened later without turning the pipes. Source: ASME B16.39 (pipe unions).

q: Which type of fitting is used for a yoke vent?
n: A yoke vent connects the soil stack up to the vent stack at an angle, so it uses a wye (45°) fitting for smooth airflow and drainage. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (yoke vents).

q: Why doesn't a water closet need a separate P-trap?
o: The trap is built into the bowl
It connects to the floor drain
n: A water closet has its trap cast into the bowl (an integral trap), so no separate P-trap is needed. Source: ASME A112.19.2 (vitreous china fixtures).

q: The trap seal is the depth of water between which two points of a P-trap?
o: The bottom of the crown weir and the inlet
The top of the dip and the crown weir
The bottom and top of the dip
n: The trap seal is the depth of water between the crown weir (overflow) and the top of the dip of the trap, normally 50–100 mm. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (trap seals).

q: Which of these has NO water-saving feature?
n: A pop-up drain only plugs the basin and saves no water. The 1.5-gallon closet, flow-limiting valve and waterless urinal all reduce use. Source: US EPA WaterSense; ASME A112.18.1.

q: What connects directly under a floor drain in a ground-floor T&B?
n: A floor drain connects directly to a P-trap below it, whose water seal keeps sewer gas out of the T&B. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (traps for floor drains).

q: Which flushing device is best for a public comfort room?
n: A flushometer (flush valve) flushes directly from a high-pressure supply and is ready immediately for the next use. That suits busy public comfort rooms. Source: ASSE 1037 (flushometers); National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: Which fitting joins two straight lengths of pipe?
n: A coupling joins two straight lengths of pipe end to end. Couplings are threaded or solvent-welded on both ends. A union is used instead where the joint must be taken apart later. Source: ASME B16.3 (threaded fittings).

q: Which is true of a sanitary tee?
o: It has a curved flow pattern
n: A sanitary tee is a drainage fitting whose branch curves into the run, directing flow downward without blocking the stack. So both statements are true. Source: ASME B16.29 / ASTM D2665 (DWV fittings); National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: What is the typical slope for a horizontal waste pipe?
n: Horizontal waste pipes slope about 2% (1/4 in. per foot) for self-cleansing flow. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (slope of horizontal drainage).

q: Which fitting is threaded on the outside and connects pipes or fittings?
n: A nipple is a short length of pipe threaded on the outside at both ends, used to connect fittings. Source: ASTM A733 (pipe nipples).

q: According to the NPC, pipe supports should be placed every __.
n: The National Plumbing Code sets maximum hanger spacings by pipe material. 1.50 m is the typical spacing quoted for small horizontal plastic pipes. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (hangers and supports).

q: T&S is the abbreviation for __.
n: On plumbing plans, T&S denotes a tub and shower combination. Source: Plumbing drafting symbols and abbreviations (ASPE).

q: WC is the abbreviation for ___.
n: WC = water closet (toilet). Source: Plumbing drafting abbreviations (ASPE); National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: On plumbing plans, FD stands for:
n: FD = floor drain on plumbing plans. A floor drain collects water from the floor surface in toilets, kitchens and service areas and carries it to the drainage system. Source: Plumbing drafting abbreviations (ASPE).

q: Where is a gooseneck spout used?
n: A gooseneck (high-arc) spout is used on sink faucets so it clears tall pots and pitchers. Source: Faucet manufacturer literature.
